1: # Mobile form decisions
2: 
3: Inspect required fields, validation rules, server responses, focus order and recovery before changing form presentation.
4: 
5: | Conditions | Candidate and trade-off | Reject when |
6: | --- | --- | --- |
7: | Short coherent form | One column, persistent labels, natural submit flow | Splitting adds unnecessary steps |
8: | Long form with meaningful stages | Sections or steps with progress and preserved values | Back loses input, validation context or deep-link state |
9: | Email/phone/numeric data | Semantic `type`, fitting `inputmode`, and correct `autocomplete` | Masking or keyboard choice blocks paste or valid formats |
10: | Validation/server error | Inline error associated through `aria-describedby`, summary/focus when useful | Error appears away from field or destroys values |
11: | Submit near viewport edge | In-flow CTA, or sticky CTA with measured clearance and keyboard handling | It obscures focused field/content or competes with system keyboard |
12: 
13: Keep labels visible; placeholders are hints. Preserve existing client and server validation, submitted values, paste, password manager behavior, zoom and success/error paths. Make email typo suggestions optional: accepting a suggestion must be an explicit user action, while declining it must not block an address that existing validation accepts. Do not lowercase an entire email address: [SMTP preserves the local part's case](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5321#section-2.4). Do not add a stricter domain rule without an existing product requirement. Use `aria-invalid` only on invalid fields; move focus deliberately after submit errors. A resized desktop viewport is not a physical keyboard test. Use the [decision contract](../decision-contract.md).

1: # Mobile Web UX Principles
2: 
3: These are **design heuristics**, not universal mandates.
4: 
5: 1. **Task-first hierarchy.** Make the primary job and its next action obvious; secondary content should not crowd it out.
6: 2. **Touch without hover.** Essential functionality must have visible, keyboard- and touch-operable controls, not hover-only affordances.
7: 3. **Browser expectations.** Respect Back, deep linking, scrolling, zoom, focus and address bar behavior.
8: 4. **Responsive content, not just columns.** Tables may need priority fields, disclosures or purposeful horizontal scroll; don't blindly make everything a card.
9: 5. **Keyboard-aware forms.** Use correct input modes, labels, validation and visible submit controls. Fixed buttons can be obscured by mobile keyboards.
10: 6. **Accessible and inclusive.** Use readable text, predictable focus order and generous hit areas; support zoom, reduced motion and long/localized labels.
11: 7. **Action discoverability.** Place frequent actions where users can find them without covering content or creating competing sticky bars.
12: 8. **Progressive disclosure.** De-emphasize optional details while keeping required information obtainable.
13: 9. **Performance is experience.** Minimize blocking JS, unexpected shifts, and interaction delays; avoid expensive decoration that hampers low-end devices.
14: 10. **Web / PWA distinction.** A browser tab and an installed standalone PWA may provide different browser controls; inspect their actual contexts.
15: 
16: ## Priority rules
17: 
18: - Fix blocked workflows before aesthetic polish.
19: - Favor familiar accessible HTML controls unless a custom component materially helps.
20: - Do not turn every site into a native app lookalike.
21: - Don't choose a pattern based solely on screen width; include the user's job and data characteristics.
22: 
23: ## Evidence requirements
24: 
25: Every material recommendation should cite an observed screen/source behavior or mark itself as a hypothesis to verify. For standards-specific claims (WCAG, browser API support) use current primary references rather than memory alone.

1: # Mobile web accessibility decisions
2: 
3: Use [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/) for normative criteria and the [checklist](../accessibility-checklist.md) for assertions. Use the [decision record](../decision-contract.md); do not claim conformance from source review alone.
4: 
5: - **Structure/labels:** associate visible labels and errors, use native buttons/links/tables where semantics fit ([1.3.1 A](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#info-and-relationships), [3.3.2 A](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#labels-or-instructions), [4.1.2 A](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#name-role-value)).
6: - **Keyboard/focus:** all controls operable by keyboard; focus visible, and the focused component is not entirely hidden by author-created content ([2.1.1 A](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#keyboard), [2.4.7 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#focus-visible), [2.4.11 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#focus-not-obscured-minimum)). Preserve logical focus entry/return for modal overlays.
7: - **Text and reflow:** support text resize and single-column reflow except genuinely two-dimensional content ([1.4.4 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#resize-text), [1.4.10 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#reflow)). Do not discard data to remove scroll.
8: - **Contrast:** normal text 4.5:1 and large text 3:1 ([1.4.3 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#contrast-minimum)); essential control indicators and focus visuals have [1.4.11 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#non-text-contrast) conditions.
9: - **Error/status:** identify an input error in text, announce status without stealing focus, expose expanded state where applicable ([3.3.1 A](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#error-identification), [4.1.3 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#status-messages), [4.1.2 A](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#name-role-value)).
10: - **Targets:** [2.5.8 AA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#target-size-minimum) requires 24×24 CSS px or one of its exceptions, including spacing; [2.5.5 AAA](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#target-size-enhanced) is 44×44 CSS px with different exceptions. Do not map native pt/dp directly to CSS px.
11: 
12: For a target-size exception, state the exact condition and measure the rendered hit areas and neighboring targets before claiming that SC 2.5.8 passes. Words such as "generous spacing" do not establish the required geometry. Passing one criterion is not proof of full WCAG AA conformance. Treat palette contrast and keyboard behavior as `NOT RUN` until tested in the rendered interface.
13: 
14: Apply these constraints to navigation, tables, forms, actions, content, overlays and touch decisions from the start. A horizontal comparison table can be valid under the two-dimensional reflow exception; maintain headers and row identity.
